heading.en: Why are there so few tigers?

hook.en: Bandipur has huge stretches of grass, many deer, and only a few tigers. Energy is lost at every step of the food chain, so the top can support only a few animals.
hook.kn: ಬಂಡೀಪುರದಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಶಾಲ ಹುಲ್ಲುಗಾವಲು, ಅನೇಕ ಜಿಂಕೆಗಳು, ಆದರೆ ಕೆಲವೇ ಹುಲಿಗಳು. ಆಹಾರ ಸರಪಳಿಯ ಪ್ರತಿ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲೂ ಶಕ್ತಿ ನಷ್ಟವಾಗುವುದರಿಂದ ತುದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲವೇ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಗಳು ಬದುಕಬಲ್ಲವು.

body.en: Except for the deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystem, the Sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. Of the incident solar radiation, less than 50 per cent is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR). Plants and photosynthetic bacteria (autotrophs) fix the Sun's radiant energy to make food from simple inorganic materials. Plants capture only 2–10 per cent of the PAR, and this small amount of energy sustains the entire living world. The flow of energy is unidirectional: from the Sun to producers and then to consumers. Ecosystems are not exempt from the second law of thermodynamics: they need a constant supply of energy to synthesise the molecules they require and to counteract the universal tendency towards increasing disorderliness.

points.en: Sun: only energy source (except deep-sea hydrothermal vents)

narration.en: Less than half of sunlight is photosynthetically active, and plants capture only 2 to 10 per cent of that. Energy flows one way, from the Sun to producers to consumers, and is never recycled.
narration.kn: ಸೂರ್ಯನ ಬೆಳಕಿನ ಅರ್ಧಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಭಾಗ ದ್ಯುತಿಸಂಶ್ಲೇಷಣಾ ಸಕ್ರಿಯ ವಿಕಿರಣ; ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು ಕೇವಲ 2 ರಿಂದ 10 ಶೇಕಡಾ ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತವೆ. ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸೂರ್ಯನಿಂದ ಉತ್ಪಾದಕಗಳಿಗೆ, ನಂತರ ಗ್ರಾಹಕಗಳಿಗೆ ಏಕಮುಖವಾಗಿ ಹರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Board: energy down a food chain

say.en: Energy enters as sunlight and flows one way along a food chain: grass, grasshopper, frog, snake.
Only about 10 per cent of the energy passes from one level to the next. From 20,000 joules in grass, the snake gets just 20.
That is the 10 per cent law. And at the very start, plants trap only 2 to 10 per cent of the photosynthetically active radiation.
Grazing food chains begin with producers; detritus food chains begin with dead matter. Working backwards: a hawk at level four with 50 kilojoules needs 50,000 kilojoules in the grass.

title.en: Food chains, trophic levels and the 10 per cent law

body.en: All animals depend on plants, directly or indirectly, for food: they are consumers (heterotrophs). Herbivores feeding on producers are primary consumers; carnivores feeding on herbivores are secondary consumers, and so on. A grazing food chain (GFC) begins with producers, for example Grass → Goat → Man. A detritus food chain (DFC) begins with dead organic matter and is made of decomposers, heterotrophic organisms (mainly fungi and bacteria) also called saprotrophs, which meet their energy and nutrient needs by degrading dead organic matter. In an aquatic ecosystem the GFC is the major conduit for energy flow; in a terrestrial ecosystem a much larger fraction of energy flows through the DFC. Natural interconnection of food chains makes a food web. Organisms occupy a specific place in the food chain, their trophic level. Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time, called the standing crop. The number of trophic levels in a GFC is restricted because energy flow follows the 10 per cent law: only 10 per cent of the energy is transferred to each trophic level from the lower trophic level.

points.en: GFC starts with producers; DFC starts with dead organic matter
Aquatic: GFC is the major conduit; terrestrial: more energy via DFC
Standing crop: living mass at a trophic level at a given time
10 per cent law limits the number of trophic levels

narration.en: A grazing food chain starts with green plants, a detritus food chain with dead organic matter. Only about 10 per cent of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next, which is why food chains are short.
narration.kn: ಮೇಯುವ ಆಹಾರ ಸರಪಳಿ ಹಸಿರು ಸಸ್ಯಗಳಿಂದ, ಡೆಟ್ರಿಟಸ್ ಆಹಾರ ಸರಪಳಿ ಸತ್ತ ಸಾವಯವ ವಸ್ತುವಿನಿಂದ ಆರಂಭವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಪೋಷಣಾ ಹಂತದ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ಸುಮಾರು 10 ಶೇಕಡಾ ಮಾತ್ರ ಮುಂದಿನ ಹಂತಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುವುದರಿಂದ ಆಹಾರ ಸರಪಳಿಗಳು ಚಿಕ್ಕವು.

problem.en: In the food chain Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Hawk, the hawk (fourth trophic level) receives 50 kJ. How much energy must the grass have fixed?

steps.en: The hawk is 3 transfers above the grass.
Each transfer passes 10%, so grass energy = 50 kJ ÷ (0.1)³ = 50 × 1,000.
